name: 420-mixedprompt-13b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1, one in-process vLLM engine. A 13B model on a single 80 GB card with no tensor-parallel argument, so tensor_parallel_size=1. 40 query heads and 40 KV heads all stay on the one device.
architecture: dense decoder (LlamaForCausalLM, 40 layers, 40 query heads and 40 KV heads -- plain MHA, no GQA -- head_dim 128, hidden 5120, intermediate 13824, float16), read off the checkpoint's own config.json. Vocabulary 32000, context window 2048. 13.0B parameters = ~26 GB of fp16 weights; KV is 2*40*40*128*2 B = 800 KiB per token, which is what limits how many sequences stay resident here. An ungated Llama-1 13B chat finetune. Its tokenizer is in the local HF cache; its weights are not, and first run downloads ~26 GB across three `pytorch_model-*.bin` shards. The repository publishes no safetensors, which is fine: this engine loads `.bin` natively and has no load-format switch.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=256, warmup 50%, bounded at 1000 requests with an 1800 s safety cap. 256 IS THE DECLARATION, not a starting guess: it is this engine's own `max-num-seqs` default and therefore the admission cap on the running batch, and a closed loop at the cap reproduces the saturated steady state an offline driver reaches by submitting everything at once, while keeping the client's outstanding set well defined. 1000 requests is the source's own `--num-prompts`. The 50% warmup and the 1800 s cap are CHOSEN, and the warmup percent is sized against `streams` rather than against the run; see chose_freely.
workload: `configs/data/sharegpt-1000-vicuna13b.jsonl`, 1000 real ShareGPT_V3 conversations, single turn each: the first human turn is the prompt and the length of the first assistant turn is the output length. This is not a synthetic approximation -- `configs/data/make-dataset.py` re-runs the era's own `benchmark_throughput.py::sample_requests` (>= 2 turns, tokenise with the served tokenizer, drop rows outside prompt >= 4 / reply >= 4 / prompt <= 1024 / prompt + reply <= 2048, then `random.seed(0)` and `random.sample(filtered, 1000)`) so the draw is REPRODUCED rather than invented. The 1000 rows carry 233094 prompt + 245124 output = 478.22 tokens per request. Prompt lengths are mean 233, median 95, p90 665, max 1024; output lengths mean 245, median 157, p90 618, max 1850 -- a wide, ragged distribution, which is the point of using the real corpus and is what `mixedprompt` in the item name refers to. THE RATIO IS THE SHAPE: 245124 generated tokens against 1000 prompts means the run is overwhelmingly decode, and the ragged output lengths mean the resident batch is a churning mixture of sequences at very different context lengths rather than a lockstep block. Sampling is part of the declaration and is the era driver's own set: temperature 1.0, top_p 1.0, top_k -1 (all tokens), n=1, no beam search, no presence or frequency penalty, no logprobs, and `ignore_eos` so every request generates exactly the row's output length. `request_format: plain` hands `sample_requests`' raw prompt string straight to the engine, applying no template.
purpose: A 13B chat assistant handling varied real-world conversations with long replies, 256 concurrent users on one GPU.
launch:
# ENGINE: vLLM at `621980bdc0d5a41e224febf962a6e0474e2b14ef`, one commit past the v0.1.3 tag
# (`git describe --tags` gives `v0.1.3-1-g621980bdc0d5`), 2023-08. This is a SOURCE CHECKOUT whose
# compiled extensions are built from that same checkout -- no PyPI wheel is involved and none can
# be. The interpreter is named by `configs/env.yaml: venv`.
#
# THIS ENGINE IS FROM 2023-08 AND ITS ARGUMENT SET IS TINY. `EngineArgs` at this commit defines
# exactly: model, tokenizer, tokenizer-mode, trust-remote-code, download-dir, use-np-weights,
# use-dummy-weights, dtype, seed, worker-use-ray, pipeline-parallel-size, tensor-parallel-size,
# block-size, swap-space, gpu-memory-utilization, max-num-batched-tokens, max-num-seqs,
# disable-log-stats. That is the whole list -- read off `vllm/engine/arg_utils.py` at the pinned
# commit, not off a later version. There is no max-model-len, no load-format, no quantization and
# no revision here; prefix caching, chunked prefill, CUDA graphs, kv-cache-dtype, compilation
# config and speculative decoding do not exist at this version either. Do not add any of them --
# an unknown key is a TypeError at engine construction, not a warning.
#
# THIS FILE IS READ LINE BY LINE as `key: value`, and a value beginning `{` or `[` is parsed as
# JSON. An indented YAML block silently never reaches the engine args, so keep every value on one
# line.

# --- THE MODEL. LlamaForCausalLM, 40 layers, 40 query heads and 40 KV heads (plain MHA, no GQA),
# head_dim 128, hidden 5120, intermediate 13824, vocab 32000, window 2048, float16 -- read off the
# checkpoint's own config.json. 13.0B params = ~26 GB of fp16 weights. KV is
# 2 * 40 * 40 * 128 * 2 B = 800 KiB per token, which at this operating point is the binding
# resource and sets how wide the running batch actually gets.
#
# Ungated, no token needed. The repository ships three `pytorch_model-*.bin` shards and NO
# safetensors; that is fine, this engine loads `.bin` natively and has no load-format switch. The
# tokenizer is already in the local HF cache; the weights are NOT and will be downloaded on first
# run.
model: lmsys/vicuna-13b-v1.3

# --- ONE GPU, ONE ENGINE. Load-bearing: this item's operating point is declared only at TP=1, and
# the quantity it reads is a per-device cost, so splitting the heads across cards would change what
# each card does per step rather than measuring the same thing twice.
tensor-parallel-size: 1

# --- PINNED AT 1. No pipeline stage boundary.
pipeline-parallel-size: 1

# --- THE CHECKPOINT'S OWN torch_dtype ("float16"), written out against default drift. `auto`
# resolves to the same thing today. Weights, activations and KV are all fp16; nothing is quantized.
dtype: float16

# --- THIS ENGINE'S OWN DEFAULT (2560), made explicit. There is no chunked prefill at this version,
# so this bounds a whole PROMPT batch and nothing else: the decode phase is bounded by max-num-seqs
# and by free KV blocks, never by this number (core/scheduler.py counts one token per running
# sequence and does not check it against this limit). It also feeds
# `prompt_limit = min(max_model_len, max_num_batched_tokens)`, and max_model_len is derived from
# config.json's max_position_embeddings (2048) because no argument can override it here. The
# request file is filtered to prompt <= 1024 and prompt + output <= 2048, so every row fits by
# construction.
max-num-batched-tokens: 2560

# --- THIS ENGINE'S OWN DEFAULT (256), made explicit, AND THE MOST LOAD-BEARING LINE IN THIS FILE.
# It is the admission cap on the running batch, and this item's operating point is declared at
# exactly this width: `scenario.json` offers 256 concurrent streams, so the scheduler is asked for
# 256 resident sequences on every step and grants as many as the KV pool holds -- see the
# gpu-memory-utilization note, which works out to roughly 120 here, so the pool binds before this
# cap does.
#
# Note `EngineArgs.__post_init__` clamps this to `min(max_num_seqs, max_num_batched_tokens)`;
# 256 < 2560, so it survives unchanged. Do not lower it without lowering `streams` with it, and do
# not raise it without saying so -- either move changes the width of the batch, which is the axis
# this setup is declared along.
max-num-seqs: 256

# --- THIS ENGINE'S OWN DEFAULT (0.90), made explicit. It decides the size of the KV pool, and the
# KV pool is what actually limits residency here: ~71.6 GiB of the card minus ~24.2 GiB of weights
# and the profiled activation peak leaves roughly 45 GiB of cache, i.e. ~59k tokens at
# 800 KiB/token, against a mean sequence of ~478 tokens. So the resident batch lands near 120 and
# well short of the 256 cap.
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.9

# --- THIS ENGINE'S OWN DEFAULT (16), made explicit. The KV block is 16 tokens = 12.5 MiB at this
# model's 800 KiB/token, so it sets the granularity the pool is handed out in. It is left at the
# default rather than tuned, and it must not differ between any two runs being compared.
block-size: 16

# --- THIS ENGINE'S OWN DEFAULT (4 GiB), written out. Pinned host memory for preemption-by-swap;
# the FCFS scheduler of this era will use it if the pool runs short.
swap-space: 4

# --- ENGINE SEED, made explicit. This is the engine's own default (0). It is passed to
# `set_random_seed` in every worker, which seeds torch, numpy and python's RNG. The workload seed
# lives in scenario.json.
seed: 0

# --- DELIBERATELY ABSENT:
#   tokenizer           -- unset means "the model".
#   tokenizer-mode      -- `auto` picks the fast tokenizer.
#   trust-remote-code   -- LlamaForCausalLM is in this engine's registry.
#   use-np-weights      -- the `.bin` shards load directly; the numpy path is a startup-time
#                          conversion cache and would change nothing about steady state.
#   use-dummy-weights   -- real weights.
#   worker-use-ray      -- not a choice at TP=1; this engine forces Ray on only above world size 1.
#   download-dir        -- the HF cache location comes from the environment.
#   --host / --port     -- the engine runs in-process under guidellm's `vllm_python` backend;
#                          there is no HTTP server.
